detailed_rationale:
Go Digit General Insurance Ltd is a digital-first non-life insurer offering motor, health, travel, property and marine cover. The company posted Q1 FY27 (Jun 2026) revenue of Rs 2,427 crore and net profit of Rs 86 crore (EPS Rs 0.93), with ROE of 12.2% and ROCE of 13.1% for the last year -- respectable, if unspectacular, returns for a general insurer. The more important signal is growth deceleration: TTM sales growth has slowed to just 7%, a sharp step-down from the 35% five-year CAGR that got the company to its IPO, most likely reflecting intensifying motor own-damage/third-party price competition and/or tighter underwriting discipline post-listing.

Profitability includes a meaningful contribution from investment/other income (Rs 472 crore), which for an insurer is a normal and recurring part of the business model (income earned on the premium float) rather than a one-off distortion, so I am not treating it as an earnings-quality red flag in the way I would for a non-financial company -- but it does mean underlying underwriting profitability is thinner than the headline net profit suggests. The stock trades at a rich 49.4x trailing earnings for a business whose growth has just decelerated sharply, and price momentum has been weak across every horizon (3/6/12-month returns all negative, trading below both 50- and 200-day averages) -- consistent with the quant model's own 'pulled back' stage-timing tag. A pending amalgamation of Go Digit Infoworks Services into the main entity (CCI-cleared, NCLT/IRDAI pending) is a related-party restructuring worth monitoring but not yet a clear positive or negative.

Reverse-DCF: 49.4x earnings for 12-13% ROE and a growth rate that has just fallen from 35% to 7% is a demanding combination -- the market is still pricing this as a high-growth digital insurer, but the most recent print looks like a business normalising toward more modest, industry-average growth. I judge the multiple rich for what the latest numbers actually show, and side with the quant Sell.
recommendation_rationale: ROE (12.2%) and ROCE (13.1%) are respectable for a general insurer, but TTM growth has decelerated sharply to 7% from a 35% five-year CAGR, price momentum is weak across all horizons, and the stock still trades at 49.4x earnings -- a valuation that assumes continued high growth the latest quarter does not support. Financial-sector leverage norms are correctly not being penalised here; the call rests on growth deceleration versus a still-rich multiple. Sell.
summary: Go Digit is a digital-first general insurer with decent, if unspectacular, profitability (around 12% return on equity), but its revenue growth has slowed sharply in the most recent year to just 7%, down from a much faster historical pace, while the stock still trades at a rich valuation and has underperformed across every recent time horizon. We rate this a Sell given the price does not yet reflect the growth slowdown.
positive_para: Go Digit has built a genuine digital-first distribution advantage in Indian general insurance, with decent underlying return ratios (12.2% ROE, 13.1% ROCE) and a business model earning recurring investment income on its premium float, which is a normal and durable feature of insurance economics rather than a one-off boost.
negative_para: TTM revenue growth has decelerated sharply to 7%, down from a 35% five-year CAGR, and the stock has underperformed across every time horizon (negative 3/6/12-month returns, trading below both its 50- and 200-day averages) -- yet it still commands a rich 49.4x trailing P/E. A meaningful share of reported profit also comes from investment income rather than pure underwriting margin, meaning core profitability is thinner than the headline number suggests.
reverse_dcf_judgment: A 49.4x P/E for a general insurer earning 12-13% ROE assumes continued high growth, but the most recent print shows growth decelerating sharply from 35% to 7% -- a business normalising toward more modest, industry-average growth rather than sustaining its earlier trajectory. I judge the current multiple rich for what the latest numbers actually show.
